newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EIB sets up 100mln ecu Hungarian debt programme.
newsitem.headline: EIB sets up 100mln ecu Hungarian debt programme.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) announced on Tuesday it was setting up a 20 bln forint (100 million ecu) Hungarian public debt issuance programme, the first of its kind in the region.
"We shall be able to tap savings in this country and convert them into finance for loans for productive investments in this country," EIB president Sir Brian Unwin told a news conference.
"What it also does is to get the EIB, which is the world's largest borrower, established in your (Hungary's) capital market," Unwin said.
In a statement, Unwin said the programme was being established "to meet an increasing demand from borrowers in Hungary for loans denominated in their national currency".
He said similiar programmes had proven successful in promoting the domestic markets of Spain, Portugal and Greece.
"We are confident we can play a similar role in Hungary and elsewhere in the region," he said.
The programme would enable the EIB to raise Hungarian forints with fixed, floating, zero-coupon or index-linked market instruments with terms ranging from one to 30 years, the statement said.
EIB vice president Wolfgang Roth said that by directly entering the Hungarian market the EIB would be able to raise funds and make available loans in Hungarian forints.

"In other words our partners will not run any risk of foreign currencies," he said, adding that the programme was important not just for the private sector but "will have a positive effect on the whole of the national economy".
"If we as a foreign institution are borrowing and lending on the Hungarian marketplace...we also contribute to the ongoing stability of the Hungarian currency," he said.
